question: According to the Census of India 2011, what is the population density of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**382/km²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the **Census of India 2011**, the population density of India is **382 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• Population density is calculated as the number of people living per square kilometer of land area.
 
• The population density of India in 2011 showed an increase from **325 persons per km² in 2001**, signifying a growth in population over the decade.
 
• Among Indian states, **Bihar** recorded the highest population density with **1,106 persons per km²**, while **Arunachal Pradesh** had the lowest density with just **17 persons per km²**.
 
• The high population density in certain regions is attributed to better economic opportunities, fertile land, and urbanization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Population Density**

 
 
• Population density is a measure of the number of people living in a unit area of land, usually expressed as persons per km².
 
• It provides insight into the spatial distribution of a population and helps in planning resource allocation and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Census of India 2011**
 
 
• It was the 15th Indian Census since 1872 and the 7th after independence.
 
• The total population of India as per the 2011 Census was **1.21 billion**, an increase of 181 million from the 2001 Census.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization and Population Density**
 
 
• Urban areas in India, such as Delhi and Mumbai, have significantly higher population densities compared to rural areas.
 
• Urbanization is driven by factors like employment opportunities, better living standards, and access to healthcare and education.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison**
 
 
• India ranks among the countries with high population density globally, alongside countries like Bangladesh and South Korea.
 
• However, regions such as Russia and Canada have significantly lower population densities due to vast land areas and smaller populations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of High Population Density**
 
 
• High population density can lead to challenges such as overcrowding, strain on resources, environmental degradation, and infrastructure issues.
 
• Proper urban planning and sustainable development are crucial to address these challenges effectively.
